text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past interactions as broad, persistent interests, giving insufficient weight to the specific purpose and recent context of the next choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they continue a specific artist, series, practical task, or clearly supported thematic interest.",
    "Related products become compelling when they add a useful capability or complement equipment users already own."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with stronger matches to recent interests, repeated needs, and specific intended uses.",
    "Similar products are treated as plausible next purchases even when they duplicate existing capabilities or require unsupported projects, equipment, dimensions, or quantities.",
    "Older or occasional interactions appear to outweigh more coherent recent behavior, producing seasonal, functional, or stylistic mismatches."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, brand, ecosystem, or general popularity substitutes for evidence of a specific reason to choose an item.",
    "Coarse similarities such as heaviness, compilation format, workshop relevance, or device family obscure differences that determine actual usefulness or enjoyment."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent intent and repeated coherent behavior provide stronger next-choice evidence than isolated historical interactions.",
    "Compatibility, ownership, meaningful upgrades, quantity, and a concrete current task determine whether related products are useful.",
    "Specific artist, premise, tone, musical style, seasonality, and recording format distinguish immediate choices from items users might consider eventually.",
    "Unidentifiable items leave relevance unresolved; uncertainty should remain distinct from evidence of dislike."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top-ranked items often satisfy broad historical similarity without establishing a specific, timely reason to choose them, crowding out more actionable matches.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked recommendations users would choose now, separated from those considered merely related or potentially useful later.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to duplication, incompatibility, unsupported use cases, unsuitable quantities, or stale interests.",
    "The relative ranking of recommendations tied to recent, repeated intent versus those supported mainly by broad category or brand similarity.",
    "The frequency of unresolved relevance judgments caused by insufficient item identity, tracked separately from explicit preference mismatches."
  ]
}
